Subject: Production latency spike - Falken.ai (us-west-2)

Marissa,

We are seeing sustained high latency and an uptick in 502/503 errors across several endpoints since ~08:55 PDT in us-west-2. P50 p95 latencies are both elevated (p95 ~1.8s) and throughput is dropping ~30%. Customers are reporting slow downs. I attached a screenshot from our dashboard and a small sample of request traces.

What we see:
- Error rate spiked to ~5.2% for generation endpoints (502/503)
- Sustained token queueing and request timeouts
- No recent deploys on our side; traffic pattern is steady but a handful of large-batch jobs started at 08:50 which correlate with the onset

Can Redwood confirm if there are any regional issues, or if you can temporarily steer traffic? This is impacting a paid milestone for us today — we need a quick mitigation path.

Attachments: falken-latency-screenshot-0806.png, sample-traces-0806.txt

Thanks,
Jorge Alvarez
Head of Site Reliability, Falken.ai

Subject: RE: Production latency spike - Falken.ai (us-west-2)

Quick triage notes from infra:
- Telemetry shows KV cache thrash on us-west-2 AZ-a and AZ-b starting at 08:49 PDT; cache eviction rates jumped and CPU on inference hosts increased ~60%.
- Error mix: ~72% are 502 gateway errors tied to overloaded inference workers, remaining are timeouts from request queuing.
- Current capacity in us-west-2 can handle baseline, but concurrent large-batch jobs are amplifying tail latency (we saw similar pattern last quarter).

Proposed mitigation (short):
1) Canary steer 15% of Falken production traffic to us-west-1 (new routing rule). This reduces sustained QPS in us-west-2 while leaving most traffic local.
2) Enable aggressive KV cache warming + short-lived pre-warming for the steer path.
3) If errors persist, expand steer to 35% and engage burst capacity (we have reserved slots but must be careful on cost).

Impacts / tradeoffs:
- Steering will cause a ~200–400ms p95 delta for steered requests but should cut 502 rates by ~70% in us-west-2 within 5–10 minutes.
- If we expand to burst capacity, it will consume committed nodes for the account regionally — informs cost/credit ask.

I’m standing by on the bridge to flip the rule once we get exec approval for the temporary steer/credit plan. Logs attached: falken-kv-metrics-0806.csv

-Rishi
Lead, Serving Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

Laura —

We have a P0 impacting Falken.ai in us-west-2. Key facts:
- Incident start: ~08:49 PDT; error rate peaked ~5.2% and throughput fell ~30% for Falken’s generation endpoints.
- Root cause (initial): KV cache saturation + worker CPU tail amplification caused by a set of large-batch jobs.
- Immediate mitigation recommended by infra (Rishi): incremental steer to us-west-1 (start at 15% -> expand as needed) and aggressive cache warming; if expanded steering or burst capacity is required we should offer a one-time credit to offset costs.

Asks:
1) Approve immediate cross-region canary steer (we will only move a small percentage to start).
2) Approve a one-time emergency credit up to $12,000 if we need to expand to burst capacity this afternoon.

Risk considerations:
- Steer will add latency for steered requests (~200–400ms p95) but will materially reduce 502s and return most of Falken’s traffic to healthy throughput.
- Customer is on a milestone today and has already escalated. We need a clear timeline and comms.

I’ll brief the customer once we have approval and the bridge is active.

—Marissa
